segments.context: The 5 lb listings lower unit price but increase exposure to staling and recipe drift if your household cannot use them in time. Stumptown and Counter Culture both tell buyers to pay attention to freshness and storage. Keep a working bag sealed, cool and dry; do not repeatedly move an opened bag into and out of the freezer. A lower per-ounce price is helpful only when the coffee is used while you still enjoy it. [8] [9]

segments.source: The roaster's Big Trouble espresso recipe uses shot time as a diagnostic, with a 25 to 35 second starting window, then asks the brewer to taste: a sharply sour result may call for a finer grind or longer ratio, while harsh bitterness may call for a coarser grind or shorter ratio. Use those as adjustments to test with your own basket and bag, not a universal pass/fail time. This is a more useful first-bag plan than copying the 1:17 filter ratio into espresso.
